headline: High: OpenMetadata can feed unstructured document content into a writable, networked processor, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP/APIs/webhooks and can surface governance/knowledge content; unstructured reads documents and processes them into text. A shared file/API bridge makes instruction-like content in documents plausible, but the pair lacks direct evidence of automatic trust or parsing of instructions, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata passes document-derived text to unstructured through a shared workspace or API bridge
IF unstructured treats extracted text as instructions or tool directives without provenance filtering
mitigations: Add a strict content/instruction separator in the handoff
Strip or neutralize prompt-like tokens before ingestion
Require human review for any document that contains executable-looking text
Use a dedicated quarantine folder for untrusted inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data, while unstructured can read files and has allowlisted network egress. If OpenMetadata exports sensitive catalog content into documents or files, unstructured may ingest and transmit it to its backend or downstream APIs. The shared-data path is plausible, but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive catalog or governance data from OpenMetadata is written into files processed by unstructured
IF unstructured sends extracted content to a remote service or API in the configured deployment
mitigations: Limit inputs to non-sensitive documents
Disable remote egress for the processing job
Redact governance and lineage fields before export
Use separate workspaces for catalog data and document parsing
requires-engineering: enforce data-class based routing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata can run multiple instances and uses MCP/APIs/webhooks; unstructured has write_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, install_packages, and allowlisted network egress. Both can mutate shared resources, so concurrent writes or package/network side effects can collide in default multi-instance deployments. The overlap is broad enough to make high the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, repo, or metadata store
IF unstructured is allowed to write outputs while OpenMetadata updates catalog state concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run each agent under distinct OS users
Disable package installation in the parsing job
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit context, lineage, and governance outputs that unstructured may consume as document text or downstream artifacts. If unstructured treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can propagate into parsed records or generated documents. There is no direct evidence of automatic action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata output is fed into unstructured without validation
IF downstream consumers trust unstructured's parsed output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Compare parsed output against source documents
Flag low-confidence fields for review
Keep OpenMetadata outputs read-only for the parser
requires-engineering: add schema validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly touches governance and memory/tribal knowledge, while unstructured processes documents and can write files. If regulated or retention-sensitive documents are routed from OpenMetadata into unstructured, mismatched retention or residency handling can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or governance records are processed by unstructured
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the catalog and document-processing stages
mitigations: Classify regulated inputs before processing
Keep retention settings aligned across both systems
Avoid routing PHI or legal records through the pair
Document deletion/export procedures for both tools
requires-engineering: implement policy-aware retention enforcement
